content: 1. The incidence of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) infections in overcrowded general wards was studied and reported in Infection Control and Hospital Epidemiology in 2008, volume 29, issue 6, pages 496–502. 2. Anderson JJ, Mokracek M, and Lindy CN described a nursing quality program driven by evidence-based practice in Nursing Clinics of North America in 2009, volume 44, issue 1, pages 83–91. 3. Virtanen M, Kurvinen T, Terho K, Oksanen T, Peltonen R, Vahtera J, and colleagues investigated the relationship between work hours, work stress, and collaboration among ward staff and the risk of hospital-associated infections among patients. This study was published in Medical Care in 2009, volume 47, issue 3, pages 310–318. 4. Pittet D, Simon A, Hugonnet S, Pessoa-Silva CL, Sauvan V, and Perneger TV examined hand hygiene among physicians, focusing on performance, beliefs, and perceptions. Their findings were published in Annals of Internal Medicine in 2004, volume 141, issue 1, pages 1–8. 5. Cunningham JB, Kernohan WG, and Rush T analyzed the relationship between bed occupancy, turnover intervals, and MRSA rates in Northern Ireland. Their study appeared in the British Journal of Nursing in 2006, volume 15, issue 6, pages 324–328. 6. The World Health Organization (WHO) published a document on natural ventilation for infection control in healthcare settings, accessible online as of October 18, 2016. 7. WHO also released global guidelines for the prevention of surgical site infections, available online. 8. A manual on decontamination and reprocessing for healthcare facilities was published by WHO and is accessible online. 9. WHO provided an infection prevention manual for construction and renovation in healthcare settings, accessible online as of October 18, 2016. 10. The fourth edition of the guidelines for drinking-water quality was published by WHO and is available online. 11. WHO developed guidelines on core components of infection prevention and control programs at the national and acute healthcare facility levels, accessible online. 12. The UK Department of Health published Health Building Note 00-09: Infection Control in the Built Environment in 2013. 13. Spaulding E discussed chemical disinfection and antisepsis in hospitals in Journal of Hospital Research in 1972, volume 9, pages 5–31. 14. WHO published the second edition of Safe Management of Wastes from Healthcare Activities in 2014, accessible online as of October 18, 2016. 15. WHO released guidelines on the use of safety-engineered syringes for intramuscular, intradermal, and subcutaneous injections in healthcare settings, accessible online as of October 18, 2016. 16. Birnbach DJ, Nevo I, Scheinman SR, Fitzpatrick M, Shekhter I, and Lombard JL proposed a quantitative method to improve hospital design for patient safety in Quality and Safety in Health Care in 2010, volume 19, issue 5, pages 462–465. 17. Koff MD, Loftus RW, Burchman CC, Schwartzman JD, Read ME, Henry ES, and colleagues demonstrated a reduction in intraoperative bacterial contamination of peripheral intravenous tubing using a novel device. This study was published in Anesthesiology in 2009, volume 110, issue 5, pages 978–985. 18. Thomas BW, Berg-Copas GM, Vasquez DG, Jackson BL, and Wetta-Hall R compared the usage of alcohol-based hand hygiene products in an intensive care unit when dispensers were placed in conspicuous versus customary locations. Their findings were published in Journal of the American Osteopathic Association in 2009, volume 109, issue 5, pages 263–267. 19. Whitby M and McLaws ML found that the accessibility of sink locations does not improve handwashing compliance among healthcare workers. This study was published in Journal of Hospital Infection in 2004, volume 58, issue 4, pages 247–253. 20. Kho AN, Dexter PR, Warvel JS, Belsito AW, Commiskey M, Wilson SJ, and colleagues developed an effective computerized reminder system for contact isolation of patients colonized or infected with resistant organisms. This study appeared in International Journal of Medical Informatics in 2008, volume 77, issue 3, pages 194–198. 21. WHO published annexes to the guidelines on core components of infection prevention and control programs at the national and acute healthcare facility levels, accessible online. 22. Holmes and colleagues conducted research projects funded by the Wellcome Trust and NIHR, focusing on antimicrobial resistance and infection management policies in critical care. These projects spanned from 2015 to 2018.
